title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 87
paragraphs: So he spoke, and Cyrus loosed his bonds and caused him to sit near himself, and paid him much regard; and Cyrus himself and all those around him marveled at the sight of Croesus. Croesus, wrapped in thought, was silent; but after a time, turning round and seeing the Persians plundering the city of the Lydians, he said: “O king, must I say to you what I happen to have in my thought, or must I keep silent in my present fortune?” Cyrus bade him say boldly whatever he wished, and Croesus asked: “What is it that this great multitude of men is doing with such eagerness?” And Cyrus said: “They are plundering your city and carrying away your wealth.” Croesus answered: “It is not my city they are plundering, nor my wealth they are carrying away, for I no longer have any property in these things. It is your wealth they are carrying and driving away.”
